A_target.statement: The set $\Q$ of [[Definition:Rational Number|rational numbers]] is [[Definition:Countably Infinite|countably infinite]].

B_source.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be [[Definition:Countable Set|countable]].
Then $A \times B$ is countable, and the image of a countable set under any mapping is countable.

object_map.reformulation: Realize Q as the image of the countable set Z x Z_(>0).

validity_conditions: Z is countable via the enumeration 0, 1, -1, 2, -2, ....
Density of Q in R does not affect countability.
proof_plan: The mapping $\Z \times \Z_{>0} \to \Q$, $\tuple {p, q} \mapsto \dfrac p q$, is a surjection.
$\Z$ is countable via $0, 1, -1, 2, -2, \ldots$, and $\Z_{>0}$ is countable.
By the source result, $\Z \times \Z_{>0}$ is countable, and so is its image $\Q$.

As $\Q \supseteq \N$ is infinite, $\Q$ is countably infinite.
{{qed}}
